explanations: The consumer dedupes on msg.id, which the broker assigns every time something is published. That catches redeliveries of the same broker message (the crash-before-ack case), but not producer retries. When checkout's publish times out after the broker already stored the event, publishPurchase publishes again and the broker creates a second message with a new id. Both pass the dedup check and the member is awarded twice. The producer already stamps every attempt with the same idempotency-key header (purchase:<orderId>), and that is the identity of the business event. Deduping on that key, falling back to the broker id for messages without one, collapses both kinds of duplicate.
